A Bring-Your-Own-Power scalable,  infrastructure-grade system that  delivers clean, continuous energy to  data centers, utilities, industrial  operations, and manufacturing  facilities.</p>

Words such as "anticipate," "believe," "continue," "could," "design," "estimate," "expect," "intend," "may," "plan,"  "potential," "project," "target," "will," "would" and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements, although not all forward-looking  statements contain these identifying words. Forward-looking statements in this presentation include, among other things, statements regarding the proposed offering and listing of the Company's  common stock; the anticipated use of proceeds; the development, engineering, construction, testing, permitting and commercialization of the Company's  HydroThermal Reactor ("HTR") technology; the anticipated performance, generating capacity, operating availability, construction costs and timelines,  efficiency, emissions characteristics and economic benefits of the HTR; the Company's ability to obtain project financing, power purchase or off-take  agreements, strategic relationships and customers; the availability of governmental incentives or tax credits; future construction activity and customer  relationships; anticipated benefits and synergies from the TRINITY acquisition; the Company's intellectual property and pending patent applications; and the  Company's other plans, strategies, opportunities and prospects. These forward-looking statements are based on management's current expectations, estimates, assumptions and projections and are inherently subject to  significant risks and uncertainties, many of which are outside the Company's control. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by the forward-looking statements as a result of numerous factors, including risks  relating to the technical feasibility, engineering, construction, testing and commercialization of the HTR; changes in design or development plans;  permitting, environmental, water-use and site-development requirements; construction costs and delays; access to financing and capital; the ability to enter  into off-take or power purchase agreements; customer adoption; competition and technological developments; energy prices and market conditions;  regulatory, tax and governmental policy changes; intellectual-property protection; TRINITY's ability to execute its backlog and obtain new projects; project  cancellations, modifications or delays; integration of TRINITY; general economic and capital-market conditions; the Company's ability to complete the  proposed offering and obtain and maintain a listing on NYSE American; and the other risks and uncertainties described under "Risk Factors" and elsewhere  in the Company's most recent preliminary prospectus and its other filings with the SEC. Forward-looking statements speak only as of the date they are made. You should not place undue reliance on these statements. Except as required by  applicable law, the Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statement as a result of new information, future  events, changes in circumstances or otherwise.</p>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">About Us One Company, Two Engines for Growth Combining next-generation clean energy technology with proven mission-critical construction expertise KiNRG, Inc. CLEAN ENERGY TECHNOLOGY KiNRG is developing a HydroThermal Reactor (HTR) &mdash;  a patented technology designed to generate reliable,  24/7 electricity using evaporative cooling and  downdraft dynamics, without combusting fossil fuels. &bull; 8 issued patents (6 U.S., plus Morocco and Kuwait),  with 5 additional applications pending &bull; Engineering and scientific team drawn from Penn  State, Georgia Tech and Duke University &bull; Developing a smaller, modular HTR purpose-built  bring-your-own-power solution for always-on data  center loads TRINITY Group Construction MISSION-CRITICAL CONSTRUCTION Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Herndon, VA,  TRINITY is a commercial general contractor delivering  preconstruction, design-build, general contracting  and construction management for data centers and  other mission-critical facilities. &bull; 2.5M+ sq. ft. of data centers built; 500K+ sq. ft. in  progress across 3 states and Egypt &bull; $657.4 million construction backlog as of July 31,  2026 + $12.4M TRINITY acquisition completed April 1, 2026 $257.2M 2025 pro forma combined revenue 8 Patents issued across the U.S. and abroad $369.2M Q2 2026 Revenue</p>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">Investment Highlights A patented energy platform paired with an established, cash-generating construction business Vertically Integrated  Strategy TRINITY builds the data center and  the power source in-house &mdash;  a bring-your-own-power   combination few competitors can  offer data center developers. Durable Customer  Relationships TRINITY services several smaller  repeat business clients, and currently  has data center construction projects  in Maryland, Virginia, Texas and Cairo.  Protected,  Differentiated  Technology The HTR is designed to generate  electricity without combusting fossil  fuels, backed by 8 issued patents  across the U.S., Morocco and Kuwait,  with 5 more pending. Large, Underserved  Market AI and data center growth is driving  unprecedented demand for reliable,  always-on baseload power beyond  what the grid can supply. Current, Cash- Generating Revenue TRINITY contributed $257.2M of FY  2025 pro forma revenue and $369.2M  of Q2 2026 revenue. TRINITY carries a  $657.4M backlog as of July 31, 2026,  funding operations while HTR is  developed.</p>
<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 6 -->
<div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</p></div>

<!-- Field: /Page -->
<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">
<p style="text-align: center; margin: 0;"><img src="ea030877201_ex99-1img7.jpg" style="width: 950px; height: 534px;"></p>
<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">How Does the HydroThermal Reactor Work? HydroThermal Reactor The HydroThermal Reactor is a concrete structure with a water  injection system at the top that introduces measured droplets  of water through a distribution header. Water Droplets The water droplets introduced near the top of the Reactor  immediately begin to react due to the sun-warmed air at the  very top of the Reactor. Evaporation The natural evaporative process immediately begins to cool  the surrounding air inside the top of the HydroThermal  Reactor. As evaporation and cooling continues, the  cooler/denser air inside the Reactor descends, reaching  speeds exceeding 50 mph. Immense Acceleration The now significantly colder, denser, damp, and compressed  air amassed near the base of the Reactor flows laterally into  tunnels surrounding the base of the Reactor, achieving wind  speeds up to and well in excess of 100 mph. A patented system of turbines extracts the kinetic energy  inside the wind tunnels and generates GREEN ELECTRICITY Patented System of Turbines</p>
<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 7 -->
<div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</p></div>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">Small Format HydroThermal Reactor Zero Carbon Footprint Eliminates ~1.5 MILLION metric tons of  carbon per installation per year if 200MW  HTR operating at baseload was being  generated by a traditional fossil fuel  power plant Supports 200 MW AI Data Center  Baseload Continuous Clean Energy  Production  24 Hours a day 7 Days a week 365 Days a year Cost-Effective Green Energy/ Green Hydrogen Solution in the  Industry Solution Based on Existing Science Replaces fossil fuels and more efficient  than solar and wind</p>

<div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</p></div>
<div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</p></div>
<!-- Field: /Page -->
<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">
<p style="text-align: center; margin: 0;"><img src="ea030877201_ex99-1img9.jpg" style="width: 950px; height: 534px;"></p>
<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">Supported by Intellectual Property Patent #8,120,191 | Efficient Energy Conversion Devices and  Methods This patent covers a novel hydraulic system capable of maintaining high efficiency  hydraulic to electric conversion under a wide variance of wind speeds, as coupled  to a plurality of wind turbines in wind tunnels. Issued 2/21/2012. USA Patent #8,517,662 B2 | Atmospheric Energy Extraction Devices and  Methods This patent covers a structure for producing electricity, specifically a Tower capable  of adding moisture at the top of the structure to hot-dry air so as to generate a  downdraft of wind within the interior of the Tower, vanes coupled to the exterior of  the Tower that at least partially define a plurality of elongated pockets to the  exterior of the Tower, and flaps located to redirect the incident wind downwards  into tunnels to convert wind to electricity. Issued 8/27/2013. USA Patent #8,643,204 B2 | Efficient Energy Conversion Devices and  Methods This patent enhances and broadens previously issued Patent #8120191. Issued  2/04/2014. USA Patent #8,727,698 B1 | Atmospheric Energy Extraction Devices and  Methods This patent claims are targeted to represent the advantages of the new Tower  structural shape, the configuration of the Tower walls, their composition as well as  the wall thicknesses for a given height, along with more efficient construction  methodology and enhanced wind force resistance over prior Tower designs. Issued  5/20/2014. USA Patent #10,989,171 | Methods and Apparatus for Storage of  Compressed Air Energy and the Release and Conversion of  Compressed Air Energy This patent relates to energy storage, and more specifically to the methods and  apparatus to harness energy when natural energy sources are not readily available,  including the storage and utilization of said energy. Issued 4/27/2021. USA Patent #11,486,359 | Multi-Stage Wind Turbine This patent covers the multi-stage wind power extractor features, including the  circular tunnel with an expanding diameter and multiple turbines aligned  inside. Each turbine has blades, a controller, and a motor. The controllers  engage the turbines based on wind speed, and the motors power generators to extract energy. USA Patent #65,031 | Multi-Stage Wind Turbine This patent covers the multi-stage wind power extractor features, including the  circular tunnel with an expanding diameter and multiple turbines aligned inside.  Each turbine has blades, a controller, and a motor. The controllers engage the  turbines based on wind speed, and the motors power generators to extract energy. Morocco Patent | Multi-Stage Wind Turbine This patent covers the multi-stage wind power extractor features, including the  circular tunnel with an expanding diameter and multiple turbines aligned inside.  Each turbine has blades, a controller, and a motor. The controllers engage the  turbines based on wind speed, and the motors power generators to extract energy. Kuwait</p>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">A wholly owned subsidiary of KiNRG, delivering mission-critical construction since 2002 ONE TEAM &mdash; 4+ YEARS OF COLLABORATION Shared Leadership, Deep Collaboration KiNRG and TRINITY share leadership and office space in Herndon, VA,  and have collaborated for over four years on integrating construction  with HTR energy technology. Founder Millard L. "Flip" Wallen, III also  serves as President of KiNRG &mdash; an alignment that culminated in  KiNRG's $12.4 million acquisition of TRINITY, completed April 1, 2026. Full-Service Construction Capabilities TRINITY Group Construction has extensive expertise in data center  development, with over 2.5 million square feet already built in the  heart of Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley and more than 500K  square feet is under construction across four data center campuses;  three located in the United States, and one globally. Regional Strength, Global Reach TRINITY serves clients throughout Virginia, Maryland, Washington, D.C.  and Texas &mdash; with active data center construction underway in three  U.S. states and Cairo, Egypt, and a growing base of repeat customers. $657.4M Construction  backlog $257.2M TRINITY 2025 total revenue 2.5M+ sf Data centers  built or  construction- managed 500K+ sf Under  construction  $369.2M TRINITY Q2 2026  total revenue ~93 TRINITY  employees (as of August  2026) TRINITY Group Construction Overview</p>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">KiNRG and TRINITY Group Construction (TGC)  Synergies Joint Ventures TGC's specialty in constructing data centers and KiNRG's focus  on powering them gives them a competitive value proposition  when bidding for contracts, supplying two essential service for  datacenters. Leverage Network TGC's previous and current projects on datacenters give KiNRG  a network of potential clients spread across several states and  countries that they would have a standing relationship with. Create New Revenue Streams TGC's build out of data centers creates an initial influx of  revenue which can create sustainable and predictable cash  flows as KiNRG supplies low-cost green energy for the  completed datacenter. Potential Upside Opportunity TCG's construction revenue currently provides growing cash  flows while KiNRG's HTR  segment provides high upside  supported by strong industry tailwinds fueled by rising  datacenter energy demand and the need for carbon-free  energy.</p>

<p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; font-size: 1px; color: White">Leadership Ron Pickett | Chairman &amp; CEO Ron Pickett, KiNRG's founder and CEO, brings over 50 years of construction, development and innovative  technology skills and expertise to the team. Mr. Pickett founded KiNRG and became its CEO on December 29,  2010. He has founded several innovative companies, including the first international telemedicine provider for  the shipping industry; a major U.S. sustainable energy, composting and recycling facility; and Telkonet, which  pioneered broadband over powerline communications and commercial energy management to the  hospitality, real estate and defense sectors. Mr. Pickett has a deep understanding of government, legislative,  and permitting practices, and has guided five companies from the startup and early stage through the public  ownership process. Additionally, Mr. Pickett served as President and a Director of internet and Wi-Fi services  provider Microwave Systems Technology Inc., and Vice Chairman of Geeks on Call Holdings, Inc., a public  company that provided quick-response, on-site computer solutions. His early career work included consulting  for Frouge and Gulf Oil on real estate deals, and later for Madison Square Garden Corporation on asset  liquidation. He earned a degree in history from Gordon College. Ron Pickett Chairman &amp;  CEO Flip Wallen President,  KiNRG CEO, TRINITY Flip Wallen | KiNRG President &amp; TRINITY CEO Flip Wallen, a 47-year veteran of the commercial real estate industry, specializes in mission-critical  construction, particularly in the data center market. A James Madison University graduate with a BBA in  Management Information Systems, he has developed over 3 million square feet of data center space in  Northern Virginia's "Data Center Alley." Flip founded TRINITY Group Construction in 2002, a leading  commercial construction company in the DC Metro area. He joined the company as Executive Vice President  of Construction &amp; Development in late 2020 and now serves as its President, advising on the integration of an  Eco-Energy Park and GH2 plant with their HydroThermal Reactor Project. www.KiNRG.com</p>
